title: Lower Investment Returns Reported by Temasek Holdings and GIC
what_it_is: Lower Investment Returns Reported by Temasek Holdings and GIC

sections.label: Questions on GIC and Temasek
sections.summary: Questions ask whether GIC and Temasek returns underperformed, affect the Net Investment Returns Contribution, and whether their mandates should be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) whether the investment returns of GIC and Temasek Holdings have underperformed the Government's expectation; (b) if so, whether there is an impact on the Government's Net Investment Returns Contribution to the Budget; and (c) what steps have been taken to ensure that the investment entities have incentives that are aligned to achieve better performance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) whether the Government has assessed the merits of a low-cost passive index-tracking investment approach for its investments; (b) whether the Government has compared this to GIC and Temasek Holdings’ active and more costly investment management approaches; and (c) if so, what are the considerations in deciding to give GIC and Temasek Holdings the investment mandates to choose the latter approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) whether the difference between GIC's investment returns and the interest payments made by the Government to the CPF Board on Special Singapore Government Securities has narrowed in tandem with the underperformance of GIC relative to other major sovereign wealth funds; and (b) if so, how will this impact the Government's fiscal position or rate of reserves accumulation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) in view of the fragmenting global geopolitical environment and its associated investment risks, whether the Government sees the need to review the current investment mandates of both GIC and Temasek; and (b) whether the emerging investment landscape is assessed to be conducive to sustaining a steady Net Investment Returns Contribution in the next decade.

sections.label: GIC 20-year real return
sections.summary: GIC achieved a real return of 3.8% per annum over the past 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: On that basis, GIC has achieved a real return of 3.8% per annum over the past 20 years.

sections.label: Temasek returns and assessment
sections.summary: Temasek reported 8% per annum Total Shareholder Return over 20 years in US dollar terms, and the Government assesses both entities' returns as reasonable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Nonetheless, over the last 20-year period, Temasek has reported a Total Shareholder Return of 8% per annum in US dollar terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Taken as a whole, the Government’s assessment is that the returns generated by GIC and Temasek are reasonable and within expectations, given their mandates and risk profiles.

sections.label: NIRC from long-term returns
sections.summary: The NIRC is derived from the expected long-term real rate of return the Reserves can sustain, not short-term market returns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: The NIRC is thus derived from the expected long-term real rate of return which the Reserves can sustain, and not short-term market returns.

sections.label: NIRC basis and smoothing
sections.summary: Net Investment Returns taken into the Budget are based on long-term expected returns, not fluctuating year-to-year returns, and the asset base is smoothed over the long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: The Net Investment Returns taken into the Government Budget every year is based on the long-term expected returns of the investment entities, not on the year-to-year returns, which can fluctuate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: In addition, the asset base that is used to calculate the NIRC is smoothed over the long term.

sections.label: GIC returns and asset disclosure
sections.summary: GIC discloses five-, 10- and 20-year returns, but total assets under management are not disclosed to avoid speculative attacks on the Singapore dollar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: GIC discloses their five-, 10- and 20-year returns, but we have spoken in this House before about how we do not disclose their total assets under management, because we do not want to encourage speculative attacks on the Singapore dollar.

sections.label: Disclosure within overall investment system
sections.summary: The principle is that entities' disclosures should be part of an overall system enabling them to maximise long-term returns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Our principle is that what the entities disclose should be part of an overall system that enables them to maximise their ability to generate long-term returns.

sections.label: GIC 20-year real return
sections.summary: GIC achieved a real return of 3.8% per annum over 20 years, within the Government's expectations given the risk profile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: GIC has achieved a real return of 3.8% per annum over the past 20 years, which is within the Government's expectations, given the risk profile that we have given.

sections.label: Benchmarks and unique context
sections.summary: Investment entities should have clear benchmarks and consider Singapore's context, including Budget returns and CPF interest obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Our investment entities should have clear benchmarks and should take into account our own unique context, including, as the Senior Minister of State mentioned, that one fifth of our national Budget is from the returns on our investments and the Government has an obligation to pay interest rates on the CPF savings.

sections.label: Threshold for NIRC framework review
sections.summary: The question asks what level of long-term returns should trigger a Government review of the NIRC framework's sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What level of long-term investment returns should be the threshold which triggers a Government review of the NIRC framework to look at its sustainability, based on new structural trends in the global investment climate?

sections.label: Alpha from GIC and Temasek
sections.summary: The question asks how the Government is convinced GIC and Temasek's active approach gives deserved alpha, amid challenging returns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How is the Government convinced that the active investment approach taken by GIC and Temasek is giving the alpha that Singaporeans deserve on the Reserves and on their CPF savings?

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: I agree with the hon Member that we should recognise that it has become more challenging to generate good investment returns in the current global environment and that this trend is likely to persist in the longer term.

sections.label: Riding out market fluctuations
sections.summary: The system lets Singapore ride out year-to-year fluctuations and sustained global under-performance due to its large asset base and long-term view.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: In fact, the system is structured such that we are able to ride out some of these year-to-year fluctuations, even periods of sustained global under-performance in markets, because we have a large asset base and because we are able to take a long-term view of our investment returns.

sections.label: GIC track record and de-risking
sections.summary: The GIC team's track record under its mandate shows it can de-risk during periods of distress such as COVID.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Overall, the GIC team has been doing so over the years and their track record, given the mandate they have been given, demonstrates that they are able to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: They have taken the decision as we talked about, to de-risk during periods of distress, during COVID, for instance, in the recent years.

sections.label: No direction on investment focus
sections.summary: The entity decides its own investment focus and local investing, as the government will not direct those decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: On the first question, I think we do not work on the basis of individual investment decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: And so, insofar as requiring them to have a specific investment focus or to invest locally, I think that is something as an entity, they need to decide and in light of the mandate that we have given them, to see whether that it is the most preferred strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: So, we will not direct it personally or directly, but we would leave them to make those decisions.

sections.label: Temasek portfolio sustainable returns
sections.summary: For Temasek's total asset portfolio, generating sustainable returns as a portfolio would be a good outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Overall, looking at the total portfolio of Temasek's assets, I think as long as it can generate sustainable returns as a portfolio, that will be a good outcome.
